decision: PROPOSED primary DEM (SDR-001 D-01); not approved
publisher: NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA); LOLA team product by M. K. Barker
version: unstated on the product page; file Last-Modified 2023-07-07T22:28:19Z
citation: Barker, M. K. et al., 2023, Planetary Science Journal 4, 183, https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data DOI 10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole
use_terms: Citation requested by PGDA: Barker et al. 2023, Planet. Sci. J. 4, 183 (doi 10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1) and data DOI 10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole. The page states no separate licence or copyright; footer points to NASA privacy and reproduction guidelines. Treated as a NASA-produced open dataset with a citation request. Not confirmed in writing by PGDA (checked 2026-11-13).
size_source: downloaded 2026-11-13; on-disk size equals the server Content-Length (2696082051)
format: cloud-optimized GeoTIFF; supports HTTP range requests (Accept-Ranges: bytes)

dem.crs: IAU 'Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric / South Polar': Polar_Stereographic, latitude_of_origin -90, central_meridian 0, false easting/northing 0, units metres
dem.reference_surface: sphere, radius 1737400 m (IAU 30100), planetocentric — read from the GeoTIFF CRS
dem.vertical_units: metres (history shows grdmath x 1000; actual_range -7296.79..7027.23 matches the PDS product's -7297..7027)
dem.nodata: declared NaN; full-file scan found 0 NaN cells (every pixel has a value), so unsampled terrain is NOT flagged by nodata
dem.pixel_registration: Area (AREA_OR_POINT=Area, node_offset=1): pixel centres lie half a pixel inside the corner transform
dem.coverage: 80S to 90S, within about 304 km of the pole (stereographic)

open_items: decide how EFFRES / ERR feed the uncertainty budget (D-01b)
optional: written confirmation of terms from PGDA

header_inspection.method: GDAL /vsicurl/ HTTP range reads of the GeoTIFF header and one 256x256 window; file not downloaded; no checksum yet

integrity.method: SHA-256 computed by the downloader and recomputed independently with sha256sum (identical)
integrity.note: A checksum proves the bytes are the ones we fetched, not that the DEM is scientifically suitable. The publisher does not provide a checksum, so this is a self-recorded pin.

full_extent_comparison_vs_pds.method: every pixel of both files on the shared 30,400 x 30,400 grid; ADJ minus PDS (DN x 0.5 m); ring = distance of the pixel centre from the pole
full_extent_comparison_vs_pds.reading: The two releases agree to about 1.5 m RMS. Rare large differences (0.0001% of pixels within 150 km exceed 100 m) mark steep terrain where the older track geolocation differs; the effect on a horizon needs a same-site horizon run on both DEMs.
